text: A prince ought to have two fears, one from within, on account of his subjects, the other from without, on account of external powers. From the latter he is defended by being well armed and having good allies, and if he is well armed he will have good friends, and affairs will always remain quiet within when they are quiet without.
author: Niccolo Machiavelli
locator: Chapter XIX, That one should avoid being despised and hated
location: Sant'Andrea in Percussina, near Florence, Italy
